result.title: ATLAS: Learning to Adapt LVLM Attention for Reasoning Video Segmentation
result.summary: Reasoning Video Object Segmentation (RVOS) aims to localize and segment objects referred to by natural-language expressions throughout a video. Although large vision-language models (LVLMs) implicitly encode localization cues in their attention maps, these attentions are often noisy, diffuse, and scattered across layers, heads, and modalities, limiting their direct use for segmentation. Existing methods typically rely on handcrafted attention-selection heuristics or computationally expensive attention refinement. We propose ATLAS, an attention adaptation framework that learns to transform raw LVLM attentions into object-centric localization cues. ATLAS treats attentions from all layers, heads, and modalities as structured features, combining high-resolution frame-level attentions that capture spatial information with low-resolution video-level attentions that encode temporal context. A lightweight U-Net equipped with temporal attention and FiLM-based modulation fuses these complementary representations to generate coarse segmentation heatmaps, which are propagated across the video using SAM2. Extensive experiments on challenging referring and reasoning video segmentation benchmarks show that ATLAS outperforms existing frozen-backbone methods. Code and models are available at \url{https://hamidreza-136.github.io/atlas/}.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 ATLAS，将 LVLM 各层、各注意力头及不同模态的注意力视为结构化特征，用带时序注意力和 FiLM 调制的轻量 U-Net 融合帧级高分辨率与视频级低分辨率注意力，生成粗分割热图，再由 SAM2 在视频中传播，用于推理式视频目标分割。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「LVLM 注意力跨层、跨头、跨模态噪声大且分散」的观察与可学习注意力聚合方式，可能为 LVR 中的视觉证据筛选及注意力结构对内部表示的影响提供核查线索，但原论文面向视频分割应用，未研究 latent 推理状态的生成。
